summary: Implemented an Ansible-driven WireGuard gateway: node1 (VyOS) terminates a WireGuard tunnel to node3; node1 NATs (masquerades) tunnel traffic toward node2; node2 runs the demo app on TCP 8080 behind a firewalld rule that only accepts connections from node1's LAN IP. node3 can reach node2:8080 only via the tunnel (direct access is rejected by node2's firewall). All work was orchestrated from node4, the pre-configured Ansible control node, using an idempotent playbook at /root/wireguard-gateway/playbooks/site.yml. All 4 nodes were restarted one at a time with proven boot-id changes and confirmed post-restart recovery.
actions_performed: Surveyed topology: node1=VyOS gateway (10.100.165.10), node2/node3=AlmaLinux9 (10.100.165.11/.12), node4=Ubuntu Ansible control node (10.100.165.13) with pre-installed ansible-core and its own SSH keypair

Bootstrapped SSH access from node4 to node2/node3 root authorized_keys, and to node1's vyos user; after discovering VyOS regenerates authorized_keys from committed config on boot, re-did the node1 key via VyOS's declarative `set system login user vyos authentication public-keys` so it survives reboots

Wrote an Ansible inventory (inventory/hosts.ini) and playbook (playbooks/site.yml) on node4: generates WireGuard keypairs on node1 and node3; configures the VyOS wg0 interface, peer, and a NAT source-masquerade rule (wg subnet -> node2) via the script-template/configure/commit/save envelope; writes wg0.conf and enables wg-quick@wg0 on node3; deploys a python3 http.server app on port 8080 as a systemd unit on node2 plus a firewalld rich rule restricting port 8080 to node1's LAN address

Diagnosed a VyOS-specific bug: running configure/set/commit as the unprivileged vyos SSH user silently fails ('without config session') because the config-session mount context isn't established for a plain user shell; fixed by enabling Ansible become (sudo to root) for the gateway host, which vyos has passwordless sudo for

Verified end-to-end: node3 reaches node2:8080 through the wg0 tunnel; after manually removing the tunnel-specific /32 route on node3, direct access to node2:8080 fails (connection refused/no route), proving the tunnel is the only path; restored the route via wg-quick and reconfirmed connectivity

Captured healthy baselines (boot_id, uptime, service/tunnel/app state) on all 4 nodes, then restarted them one at a time (node1, node2, node3, node4) via native reboot, polling until each came back, confirming a changed boot_id each time, and re-verifying service health, WireGuard tunnel state, NAT config persistence, firewalld rule persistence, and full tunnel connectivity after each restart
Re-ran the Ansible playbook after all restarts to confirm idempotency (no unintended changes) and working SSH connectivity to all managed nodes

evidence.requirement: Application served from node2 on TCP 8080
evidence.summary: systemd unit wg-demo-app.service runs python3 http.server on 0.0.0.0:8080 on node2; content served and confirmed reachable

evidence.requirement: node3 reaches the app only through a WireGuard tunnel terminated on node1
evidence.summary: wg0 on node1 shows an established peer/handshake with node3; node3's curl to node2:8080 succeeds over the wg0-routed path; after deleting the tunnel-specific route, direct access from node3's real IP fails with 'No route to host' (firewalld reject), and access is restored once the wg0 route returns

evidence.requirement: Implementation via Ansible from the control node
evidence.summary: Inventory and playbook authored and executed from node4 (the designated control_node with ansible-core installed); playbook applies all WireGuard/NAT/app/firewall configuration across node1/node2/node3 and re-runs idempotently

evidence.requirement: VyOS config-session bug diagnosis and fix
evidence.summary: Isolated the failure to the vyos user's SSH session lacking a valid config session; confirmed sudo/root context resolves it, then wired become:true into the gateway play, producing a clean 'no configuration changes to commit' / successful apply

evidence.requirement: node1 restart evidence (baseline, restart ack, changed boot id, recovery)
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 01e92881...; reboot acknowledged; new boot_id c5b68ddb... with 22s uptime; wg0 interface, peer config, and NAT rule all intact post-restart; node3 tunnel access confirmed working after node1 restart

evidence.requirement: node2 restart evidence (baseline, restart ack, changed boot id, recovery)
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id f54d7366...; reboot acknowledged; new boot_id a7d3bc82... with 4s uptime; wg-demo-app.service active and firewalld rich rule intact post-restart, app responds locally

evidence.requirement: node3 restart evidence (baseline, restart ack, changed boot id, recovery)
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id dfdea52d...; reboot acknowledged; new boot_id 1bb5c3ca... with 5s uptime; wg-quick@wg0 active, tunnel route restored automatically, app reachable through the tunnel post-restart
